sentences.text: Procurement has the order form for 144 seats - shall we walk their questions?
To be honest, at 144 seats you are on the mid tier, so let me show you both.
Between us, the data cleanup is usually the work people underestimate before launch.
Is this being recorded?
I want to send it to the people who could not make it - I can check the exact figure.
We can run the migration against a copy of your data first, so nobody is guessing at go-live.
Security review is the gate the COO worries about, not the price.
When v1.2.1 went out, how did you know before your customers told you - does that work for you?
We would need a 12 month term rather than an annual one.
The thing is, if Vidhi leaves, does anyone else at Quillen Press know how this is configured?
Yep, that works.
I will confirm whether the COO signs off or someone else does.
I mean, is the $80,000 number the renewal or the renewal plus the add-on?
We are still comparing you and the tool their US team already uses internally.
How much of the onboarding is your team and how much lands on mine?
The COO wants a written comparison before we decide.
Our own p95 budget is 1004 ms; where does yours sit under that load?
How does onboarding look if we start in the new fiscal year?
Let - let me get the COO whatever the security review needs.
Vidhi, customers your size move cost per transaction inside a quarter; beyond that it is your process, not us.
I can bring a solutions engineer to the transaction dispute form session.
Realistically, the transaction dispute form limit is per-project, not per-account - that usually changes the sizing.
The failure mode there is a retry, not a dropped record; I can send you what the queue does.
Then let us aim at a decision date rather than a start date - the end of the month?
Ok, so we can pin Quillen Press to eu-west-1 - it is a setting, not a migration project.
What do you think, Vidhi?
For what it is worth, I will send the transaction dispute form write-up and the pricing in one email, not three.
Sorry, if the eu-west-1 answer holds, the rest of this is straightforward for Quillen Press.
